_comment: 4-tier skill classification — programs are the main line; skills exist in 4 tiers to verify, judge, debug, or handle NL-only tasks. Skills whose content is replicable by deterministic code get ported to programs and deleted.

verification.description: Run AFTER program PASS to spot-check the deterministic output. AI MUST invoke before claiming PASS to user.

judgment.description: Programs cannot determine subjective quality. AI invokes when output needs domain interpretation.

debug.description: Programs FAIL → AI close-loops via debug skill. Triggered automatically when runner returns FAIL.

nl_primary.description: No deterministic equivalent exists. AI invokes directly when user intent matches.

deprecated_skills._comment: Skills already replaced by deterministic programs and archived under .deprecated_skills/.

unbuilt_skills._comment: Skill names the canonical flow ROUTED TO that were never authored -- distinct from deprecated_skills, which were built and archived on purpose. Recorded rather than silently deleted so a step advertising work the tree cannot do stays VISIBLE and cannot quietly return. status=gap means no shipped skill covers that step's AI half and the step now declares none; status=covered means a shipped skill (or the deterministic track that replaced the name) serves it and the step routes there now. Enforced by programs/tests/test_fallback_skill_routes_to_a_shipped_skill.py: no name listed here may appear in flow/phase1_phase2_phase3.yaml, ship under skills/, or also be listed under deprecated_skills. If one is ever BUILT, delete its entry here in the same change.

cdc-check.note: CDC triage. Step 3's deterministic half is complete and wired (cdc_crossing_check, cdc_async_input_check, clock_domain_reg_crossing_check, reset_dependency_check); no shipped skill covers CDC triage. rtl-repair is the nearest and is not it -- it covers lint/synth/sim-mismatch, not clock-domain crossing.

rdc-check.note: RDC triage. Same step and same finding as cdc-check; reset_dependency_check is the deterministic half.

fpga-test-harness.note: Named by two steps. Step 6 now routes to fpga-led-probe-allocation, which that step's own program entry cites by path ('fpga_led_probe_lint ... Enforces the four LED-probe anti-patterns of skills/fpga-led-probe-allocation'); step 39 already named fpga-signaltap. The wrapper-emitting bring-up SKILL the flow comment refers to ('an AGENT-INVOKED board bring-up helper (skill `fpga-test-harness` above)') was never authored; fpga_test_harness_gen is the program and is deliberately not auto-wired.

constraint-gen.note: SDC + PVT authoring. sdc_gen.py and pvt_matrix_check.py exist as programs but step 7 declares NO programs and NO mcp_tools, so this ghost was its only declared executor. No shipped skill covers constraint authoring.

sdc-validator.note: Ported to a program of the same name: sdc_validator_check.py, already declared and wired on step 8. The skill half was never authored.

dft-insert.note: Scan insertion. Deterministic half wired (eda_dft, bsdl_emit, dft_signoff_check); no shipped skill covers DFT insertion.

atpg.note: Deterministic half wired (fault_atpg_run, dft_atpg_coverage_check); no shipped skill covers ATPG coverage triage.

cts-plan.note: Clock-tree planning. Deterministic half wired (clock_plan_check, and cts_quality_check exists); no shipped skill covers CTS planning. sta-review is the nearest and covers timing triage, not clock-tree construction.

placement-optimize.note: ppa-optimize ships and its description is this step's job verbatim: 'bounded, reversible actuator moves ... placement density, clock period, synthesis effort, buffering, floorplan aspect'.

em-check.note: ir-drop-triage ships and is the EM skill under its shipped name: 'Triage static and dynamic IR-drop and electromigration (EM) reports from power signoff tools'.

perc-check.note: Recorded history, in the flow's own words on this step: 'the PERC skill was named with NO PERC program behind it'. The PROGRAM half has since landed (perc_corpus_sweep, perc_signoff_check); the SKILL half never existed. drc-fix and lvs-triage both ship and remain declared on step 31.

power-analysis.note: ppa-measure ships and reads exactly this step's artefact: 'Read PPA artefacts that the tools already wrote -- STA reports, power reports, area reports'. power_total_vs_budget_check computes the verdict it reads.

stage_axis._comment: WHERE IN THE FLOW EACH SKILL APPLIES. The axis is the flow's own `stage:` field -- the eight values declared in flow/phase1_phase2_phase3.yaml -- plus two values that are NOT flow stages and must never be added to the flow's `stages[]`: `stage_all` and `off_flow`. NO FOURTH MAPPING: a skill NAMED BY A STEP (in that step's `skills:` or its stage's `on_pass_review:`) inherits that step's stage by DERIVATION and MUST NOT be listed here -- listing it would be the second declaration that flow_stage_membership_single_declaration_check exists to prevent. This block declares ONLY skills no step names. Enforced by programs/skill_stage_membership_check.py.
stage_axis.stage_all_is_a_claim_not_a_bucket: `stage_all` asserts a skill is worth invoking at EVERY stage -- stage1 AND stage3 AND stage5_manufacturing AND stage_analog. Multi-stage is NOT all-stage: a skill that applies at four of eight is listed at those four. A skill that cannot be placed is UNDECIDED and must be reported as such, never parked in stage_all.
stage_axis.off_flow_is_also_a_claim: `off_flow` asserts the skill's SUBJECT is the plugin, the repository, the CI or the benchmark programme -- not a design passing through the flow. It is falsifiable by reading what the skill reads and writes: if it operates on a design's artefacts it is not off_flow. This value exists because the 41 did NOT split cleanly into stage/stage_all, and forcing a repo-maintenance loop into stage_all would have made that value meaningless -- the same reasoning that produced `unbuilt_skills`.

spec-review.why: Reviews the NL spec for ambiguity BEFORE it enters spec-to-rtl -- it reads a spec and no RTL exists yet.

spec-validator.why: Cross-checks Datasheet / Application Note / Spec for consistency, which is phase-1 document work -- but its section 4 is 'spec_conformance_check.py -- Spec<->RTL contract gate (once RTL exists)' and runs `--rtl-dir phase2/stage1/rtl --top <module>`, and its procedure step 4 is 'Once RTL exists, run spec_conformance_check ... to prove the RTL conforms to the spec's ports + reset + latency contract'. That half reads stage1's artefact, so the skill is genuinely multi-stage. Found by spot-checking stage_phase1 against what each skill READS rather than what its name suggests.

phase1-completeness-deep-review.why: Its own description: runs 'After phase1_one_shot_runner emits L*.json' and checks every input fact landed in an L-doc.

phase1-coverage-loop.why: Measures input->L1-L27 token completeness; its subject artefact is the L-doc set.

checkpoint-gate.why: Triggers at the Phase 1->2 and Phase 2->3 transitions, i.e. it gates the EXIT of stage_phase1 and of stage2. Two named transitions -- multi-stage, deliberately NOT stage_all.

architecture-explore.why: Micro-architecture trade-offs 'before committing to RTL' -- it feeds the stage that authors RTL.

ppa-predict.why: Explicitly 'EARLY, PRE-SYNTHESIS ESTIMATE ... before any tool has run', so it sits before stage2 synthesis.

catalog-glue-author.why: Invoked when design_one_shot_runner.step_rtl_gen waives; it writes into phase2/stage1/rtl/.

hls-c2rtl.why: C/C++/SystemC -> synthesizable RTL: an alternative front end to the RTL-authoring stage.

rtl-repair.why: Fixes lint violations (stage1) and synthesis errors (stage2); its inputs are RTL and tool logs from both.

design-for-eco.why: Spare-cell insertion happens 'after placement, before CTS' -- inside the physical stage.

ppa-recover.why: Bounded way out when a PPA closure loop has stalled or oscillated; the closure loop it names is PnR.

eco-plan.why: A late-stage change to an ALREADY-placed-and-routed netlist; it cannot apply before that netlist exists.

phase3-backend-verify.why: Its own description: runs after 'synth netlist + DEF + GDS + STA + DRC reports' exist. On-pass reviewer for the backend stages.

ppa-diagnose.why: Explains why a PPA number is where it is, starting from the deterministic diagnosis; those numbers first exist at synthesis and are re-measured post-layout.

fpga-hps-bridge.why: FPGA verification plumbing; the flow's two FPGA steps are step 6 (stage1) and step 39 (stage4).

hw-debug-loop.why: Invoked after the SOF is burned and real-silicon connect_test FAILs -- it needs a programmed board.

scope-pattern-attestation.why: Probes REAL SILICON IO over SCPI; applies once hardware exists, i.e. on-board sign-off and post-silicon.

yield-diagnostic.why: Reads ATE / wafer-sort data and wafer maps -- artefacts that exist only after fabrication and test.

analog-sizing.why: Transistor sizing against analog specs; step A4 of the analog track.

analog-hw-testbench-gen.why: FPGA RTL for hardware-in-the-loop ANALOG testing; part of the analog HIL track.

analog-hw-measure.why: Scope capture + FPGA ADC read for analog blocks; the analog HIL measurement step.

benchmark-enhancement-capture.why: Its own description makes the all-stage claim explicitly: 'Applies to EVERY step in the Vibe-IC flow: Phase 1 NL ingestion, Phase 2 ..., Phase 3 ..., Analog A1-A9, Mixed-Signal M1-M4, MCP-EDA tools, and benchmark harness itself.' A recovery worth absorbing can happen at any stage.

community-backlog-submit.why: 'Invoke at any point during Phase 1/2/3 when you discover a gap.' The trigger is discovering a plugin gap WHILE RUNNING A DESIGN, which can occur at every stage -- unlike the maintenance loops below, which are not invoked from inside a design run at all.

core-agent-loop.why: Polls the repo for open issues and ships fixes; invoked as a cron on the REPO, never from inside a design run.

gatekeeper-loop.why: Gates and lands PRs on main. Its subject is the repository.

field-agent-loop.why: Drives plugin quality by running benchmarks and filing issues; its subject is the plugin.

fork-gatekeeper-loop.why: Maintains the forked EDA/PDK repos and the composed image. Its subject is other repositories.

loop2converge.why: Converges a benchmark subject by fixing the plugin layer that owns each FAIL; its output is a PR to the plugin.

regression-issue-fix.why: Fixes Phase-1 picker/extractor REGRESSIONS in the plugin's own code, not in a design.

regression-manage.why: CI / nightly regression orchestration and flaky-test triage. Its subject is the test infrastructure.

flow-change-acceptance.why: The acceptance standard for changing THE FLOW ITSELF -- a gate, a step, a verdict rule. It is read by someone editing the plugin.

layer-contract-doctrine.why: Read BEFORE authoring or revising an L-layer emitter, schema field, or gate. It governs plugin authoring, not a design's progress.

full-test-audit.why: The plugin's own four-part health check (suite + D1/D2/D3). Its subject is the plugin tree.

open-benchmark-methodology.why: Doctrine for how a benchmark NUMBER must be produced. It constrains measurement methodology, not a point in a chip's flow.

benchmark-verify.why: Produces BENCHMARK_VERIFICATION_REPORT.md for a benchmark IC. Owner ruling 2026-08-30: this is a BENCHMARK artefact -- it belongs to the benchmark programme, not to a stage of the flow.

ppa-benchmark.why: Sets up a PPA comparison between ARMS (tool versions, flow configurations, PDKs). Its subject is a comparison between runs, not a stage within one.

ppa-distill.why: Turns a PPA recovery into a reusable case and drafts the deterministic rule it should become -- a plugin-improvement capture.
